experiment: Three independent runner SHA-verified native read cost with old TAGS and TimeRanges retained after historical SAMPLES partition drop

binary.optimization: O1 stock, glibc, no C++ patch

fixture.historical_samples_removed_by: explicit DROP PARTITION, an exact physical retention model; not an actual asynchronous TTL event

protocol: Same stock-O1 binary/schema for clean 2k active-only and aged 2k identical active+48k retired ID tables. Historical SAMPLES partition dropped only from aged. Same native full label/time/numeric oracle for both. For each broad and p0 selector, 4 phases clean/aged/aged/clean with 3 warmups +10 measured per phase, QueryFinish CPU/read_rows/read_bytes/memory, 25% A/A p50 wall/CPU drift bound. All three GitHub runner jobs use same script hashes, binary and fixture.

reducer.note: Official GitHub ZIP digests checked independently before repacking ZIPs for parser; reducer report keeps local repacked hashes.

known_negative.reason: No ClickHouse server start step, refused TCP; no metric or correctness measurement

source_proof: src/Storages/StorageTimeSeries.cpp ## Retention explicitly says TAGS has no TTL by default even when all samples are deleted. tags_deduplication_cache_expiration_seconds is an in-memory cache setting, not a disk retention rule.
math_bound: For K=400 three-hour node slots, new IDs/day=400*24/3=3200 per metric; 15d live=48000, 365d historical=1168000 if no expiry. Synthetic 25x ID ratio (50k total/2k live) yields a measured 17x native read_rows and +42.8% broad p50, but extrapolation to 1.16m IDs is unsafe without heldout fixture and production-like cache/part layout.
limitations: Old SAMPLES were manually removed using DROP PARTITION; this proof does not exercise the actual TTL background scheduler or whether it purges TAGS automatically (source documents that it does not by default).
One metric, finite gauges, two query shapes, unique one-point per ID; not full 14d or 1.33m live high-cardinality production workload.
No concurrent inserts while querying; TAGS/TimeRanges static after OPTIMIZE FINAL. Retired record lifecycle and late-arrival semantics unresolved.
Only unmodified stock O1/glibc ClickHouse, no optimized jemalloc release or comparison with VictoriaMetrics.
A persistent TAGS row is not itself incorrect and should not be deleted automatically without semantics/provenance. The observed cost is workload-specific.
